column1: # mux-standby-32 — per-row leg shares, forward = client->exit, reverse = exit->client

column2: carrier.tsv counts a TRANSPORT, not a route group: a transport another group or app also rides counts that traffic here too
latency_ms is the end-of-set legs.json snapshot, not the latency measured on the row

shares and verdicts are computed over the legs that carried the payload: every leg of an ACTIVE group, plus any leg holding >= 1 % of the payload-direction bytes of the row (a mid-set promotion the set-start role does not yet show); the rest are listed with their bytes and a "-" share
some legs are in scope on bytes alone: their group reads "standby" in the set-start legs.json but they carried >= 1 % of the payload of a row
rev_bytes/rev_share on 19 row(s) are the EXIT's OWN per-leg sent_bytes deltas (rev_basis exit-sent) — the reverse direction measured at the SENDING end

rev_bytes/rev_share on 1 row(s) are the local recv_delta (rev_basis local-recv): the exit's sent_bytes needs a per-row EXIT_SNAP run against an exit that reports the per-leg byte counters, and either the snapshots or the counters were absent
